propertyFacts.label: Active phosphorus precursor consumption
propertyFacts.value: The source reports that active transaminated aminophosphine signals near 112/98 ppm disappear over the first approximately 10 min. Signals near 14/11 ppm persist in Figure 5 and are assigned to tautomers of the active transaminated precursor. The 30 ppm signal is phosphonium salt; the 18 ppm signal is proposed aminophosphine oxide.

propertyFacts.label: Source yield normalization
propertyFacts.value: Raw yield estimates can exceed 100% for 0 and 0.25 equivalent EDTA because of optical/volume assumptions, organic absorption and scattering. Main plots normalize the maximum to 100%; this is not an absolute conversion or isolated mass yield.

propertyFacts.label: EDTA loading effect on growth and yield
propertyFacts.value: Across the EDTA series, higher EDTA decreases initial InP growth rates and relative optical yield; unprinted graph values remain source images.

facts.label: Active phosphorus precursor consumption
facts.value: The source reports that active transaminated aminophosphine signals near 112/98 ppm disappear over the first approximately 10 min. Signals near 14/11 ppm persist in Figure 5 and are assigned to tautomers of the active transaminated precursor. The 30 ppm signal is phosphonium salt; the 18 ppm signal is proposed aminophosphine oxide.

facts.label: Source yield normalization
facts.value: Raw yield estimates can exceed 100% for 0 and 0.25 equivalent EDTA because of optical/volume assumptions, organic absorption and scattering. Main plots normalize the maximum to 100%; this is not an absolute conversion or isolated mass yield.

facts.label: EDTA loading effect on growth and yield
facts.value: Across the EDTA series, higher EDTA decreases initial InP growth rates and relative optical yield; unprinted graph values remain source images.

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
